subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Adapted from the school Drive Quran folder (TPS Quran Tracker: Reception Qaidah/Quran columns, tajweed rules by year); Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf (Hafs)

lessons.title: The Qur'an is Allah's words
objectives: Know that the Qur'an is the book of Allah
Show good manners (adab) with the Qur'an
Say Bismillah correctly after the teacher

keywords.def: the words of Allah, sent to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
In the name of Allah
good manners

starter: Say 'Bismillah' with me. What do we say before we start something good?
Show your best listening ears. Where are they?
Can you point to the Qur'an picture on the screen?

teach.heading: Allah's special book
bullets: The Qur'an is the words of Allah
Allah sent it to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
teach.note: Hold up a mushaf or show a clear picture. Keep it simple: Allah spoke it, Jibril brought it, the Prophet ﷺ taught it. Ask: who gave us the Qur'an? Accept 'Allah'.

teach.heading: Good manners with the Qur'an
bullets: Clean hands before we touch it
Hold it carefully, not on the floor
teach.note: Model each action. Tell children that being clean and in wudu is best and older classes will learn the rulings; for now the focus is care and respect. Misconception: the Qur'an is 'just a book' - stress it is Allah's speech.

teach.heading: Our first words: Bismillah
bullets: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful
We say it before we begin
teach.note: Say one phrase at a time, children echo. Echo-recite slowly twice. Clap the beats: Bis-mil-lah-ir-rah-maa-nir-ra-heem. Do not rush; accuracy of sound matters more than speed.

teach.heading: Listening game
bullets: Echo back exactly what you hear
Lips closed while listening, then say it
teach.note: Teacher recites Bismillah in short chunks; children echo. Praise accurate echoes by name. Gently re-model any child who changes a sound; do not correct harshly.

practice: Echo: 'Bismillah' in three chunks: Bismillah - ir-Rahmaan - ir-Raheem
Show me how we hold the Qur'an carefully (act it out)
independent: Colour the picture of the Qur'an and write or trace 'Bismillah' in English letters
Match the manners cards: clean hands / hold carefully / sit quietly (tick the good ones)
Draw yourself listening to the Qur'an
exit: What do we say before we start?
lessons.homework: Tell your family one good manner with the Qur'an and say Bismillah before your meal.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use picture cards and gesture for each manner. Stretch: recite Bismillah alone to a partner.

lessons.title: Listening to Al-Fatihah (ayat 1-3)
objectives: Listen carefully to Al-Fatihah ayat 1-3
Echo the ayat with the teacher
Know a simple meaning of each ayah

keywords.def: the Opening, the first surah of the Qur'an
one verse of the Qur'an
a chapter of the Qur'an

starter: Say Bismillah. What is the Qur'an?
Show a good listening position.
What do we call one verse of the Qur'an? (ayah)

teach.heading: The Opening surah
bullets: It is the first surah in the Qur'an
We read it in every prayer
teach.note: Explain that Muslims recite Al-Fatihah in every rak'ah of prayer. Show seven fingers for seven ayat. Reception children learn by ear first; reading comes later.

teach.heading: Ayah 1 and 2
bullets: All praise is for Allah, Lord of all the worlds
teach.note: Recite ayah 2 in two chunks: 'Al-hamdu lillaah' / 'Rabbil-'aalameen'. Meaning: we thank Allah because He made and looks after everything. Ask what they thank Allah for.

teach.heading: Ayah 3
bullets: The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful
Allah is kind and loving to us
teach.note: Link back to Bismillah: the same two names. Ask: which words did we already hear in Bismillah? Praise anyone who notices the repeat.

teach.heading: Echo and repeat
bullets: Then we say it all together
teach.note: Use call and response, three rounds. Slow, clear, mouth shapes visible on camera. Stop before children tire; 30-minute attention is short.

practice: Echo 'Al-hamdu lillaah' five times, getting clearer each time
What does 'Al-hamdu lillah' mean?
independent: Join in with ayat 1-3 as a class, then in pairs
Draw something you thank Allah for and say 'Alhamdulillah'
Sticker game: put the three ayat in order from picture cards
exit: Which surah did we listen to today?
lessons.homework: Listen to Al-Fatihah ayat 1-3 with a grown-up three times this week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: allow whole-body actions for each ayah and repeat in short chunks. Stretch: recite ayat 1-3 from memory.

lessons.title: Al-Fatihah (ayat 4-7)
objectives: Echo ayat 4-7 of Al-Fatihah
Know the meaning of 'You alone we worship'
Say all of Al-Fatihah with help

keywords.def: doing things only to please Allah
show the right way
the right way that leads to Jannah

starter: Say ayat 1-3 of Al-Fatihah together.
What does 'Alhamdulillah' mean?
How many ayat are in Al-Fatihah?

teach.heading: Ayah 4 and 5
bullets: Owner of the Day of Judgement
You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help
teach.note: Meanings only in simple words. 'Day of Judgement' = the day Allah will judge everyone. Stress we ask Allah alone for help; link to making du'a when we need something.

teach.heading: Ayah 6
bullets: Guide us to the straight path
We ask Allah to show us the right way
teach.note: Draw a straight road on the board and a wobbly one. Ask which is easiest to follow. The straight path is Islam.

teach.heading: Ayah 7
bullets: صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ
The way of those You blessed
Not those who went the wrong way
teach.note: This is the longest ayah. Chunk it into four parts and echo. Keep the meaning very simple: the path of the good people Allah blessed.

teach.heading: Put it together
teach.note: Recite all seven with the class; children join where they can. Note who needs extra help and record on the tracker (1 = started, 2 = most, 3 = secure).

practice: Echo ayah 5 in two halves
What do we ask Allah for in ayah 6?
independent: Join in with the whole surah in a circle: each child says one chunk
Draw the straight path to Jannah
Teacher listens to individuals say ayah 2 and ayah 6
exit: Why do we say Al-Fatihah in every prayer?
lessons.homework: Say Al-Fatihah with a grown-up each day, even if you only know some of it.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: pair with a buddy; accept partial recitation and celebrate it. Stretch: recite all seven ayat alone.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Arabic letters and their sounds
lessons.title: Letters: alif, baa, taa, thaa
objectives: Recognise ا ب ت ث
Say the sound of each letter
Spot the dots: none, one, two, three

keywords.def: the 28 letters we use to read the Qur'an
a small mark above or below a letter

starter: Say Bismillah. Echo 'Al-hamdu lillaah'.
Which surah did we listen to last week?
Clap three times for three dots.

teach.heading: Alif (ا)
bullets: Alif is a tall straight line
teach.note: Draw alif in the air. Alif's sound depends on the vowel on it; for now we learn the name and shape. Do not teach 'alif = a' as the fixed sound; say we will learn more soon.

teach.heading: Baa (ب) and Taa (ت)
bullets: Baa says 'b' like bat; taa says 't' like tap
teach.note: Show the shapes on the board. Chant 'baa one dot below, taa two dots above'. Check the lips close for baa. Use the finger-on-the-lips trick.

teach.heading: Thaa (ث)
teach.note: Show the tongue between the teeth on camera. Many children say 's' or 't' instead of 'th'. Model slowly, let them copy in a mirror.

teach.heading: Same shape, different dots
bullets: ب ت ث have the same body
Count the dots to know the letter
teach.note: Hold up three cards. Ask: how many dots? Which letter? Reinforce that dots are important in Arabic - they change the letter completely.

practice: Point to the letter with one dot below
Say the sound of ت and ث
independent: Letter hunt: find ب ت ث in a row of letters
Trace ا ب ت ث on a worksheet or in rice/sand
Sort picture cards: bat, tap, think by first sound
exit: Which letter has one dot below?
lessons.homework: Find the letter baa, taa or thaa on a packet or sign at home and show us next time.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use large letter cards and multisensory tracing. Stretch: write the four letters unaided.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Arabic letters and their sounds
lessons.title: Letters: jeem, Haa, khaa, daal, dhaal
objectives: Recognise ج ح خ د ذ
Say the sound of each letter
Tell the dot patterns apart

keywords.def: a letter said from the throat or the back of the mouth
a letter with a 'th' sound like 'this'

starter: Say the sounds of ا ب ت ث.
Which letter has three dots above?
Show me a tall straight line (alif).

teach.heading: The jeem family
teach.note: These three share a body shape; only the dots change. Chant 'inside, none, above'. Jeem is a 'j' as in jam; do not call it 'g'.

teach.heading: Haa and khaa sounds
bullets: ح: breathy 'h' from the middle of the throat
خ: rough sound from the back of the throat
Like a soft cough or clearing the throat
teach.note: Demonstrate lightly; do not strain. Haa is a breathy h with no voice, like fogging a mirror. Khaa is like Scottish 'loch'. Praise attempts.

teach.heading: Daal and dhaal
bullets: ذ dhaal: one dot, says 'th' as in this
Neither letter joins to the next letter
teach.note: Show the little curved shape. Compare 'dog' and 'this'. Mention only that they do not join; full joining is taught in Year 1.

teach.heading: Sound chant
teach.note: Rapid-fire call and response. Mix the order so children listen rather than recite from rote.

practice: Point to the letter with a dot above the curved shape
Say the sound of ذ
independent: Letter bingo with ج ح خ د ذ
Trace the five letters
Say the letter, then clap its sound
lessons.homework: Practise saying ج ح خ د ذ to a family member, asking them to point.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: pair each sound with a picture (jam, khubz, dog, this). Stretch: choose which letters look alike and why.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Arabic letters and their sounds
lessons.title: Letters: raa, zay, seen, sheen
objectives: Recognise ر ز س ش
Say the sound of each letter
Match letters to their dot count

keywords.def: the 'r' sound, tongue taps the roof lightly
the 's' sound

starter: Say the sounds of ج ح خ د ذ.
Which letter has three dots above?
Which two letters never join forward?

teach.heading: Raa (ر) and Zay (ز)
bullets: They look like small curved lines
teach.note: Raa is a rolled/tapped r. Zay is 'z' as in zebra. Draw both on the board. Same body, a dot makes the difference.

teach.heading: Seen (س) and Sheen (ش)
bullets: س seen: three teeth, no dots
ش sheen: three teeth, three dots above
teach.note: Count the teeth with fingers. Ask how many dots sheen has. Note that س and ش look the same except for the dots.

teach.heading: Clear and careful sounds
teach.note: Mimic: sssnake, shhh, zzzebra. Check the child's teeth and tongue positions.

teach.heading: Letter pairs game
teach.note: Teacher says a sound; children hold up the right card. Slow down; repeat each sound twice.

practice: Hold up the card for sheen
Which letter has one dot above and looks like a small curve?
independent: Sorting: put ر ز س ش into 'dots' and 'no dots'
Trace and say each letter
Play 'I spy' with letter sounds
exit: How many dots does sheen have?
lessons.homework: Say the sounds of the four letters to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: link each sound to a sound-story action. Stretch: find a word in English that starts like each letter.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Arabic letters and their sounds
lessons.title: Letters: Saad, Daad, Taa, DHaa (heavy letters)
objectives: Recognise ص ض ط ظ
Say these as 'big mouth' (heavy) letters
Tell them apart from light partners

keywords.def: a letter said with a full, deep mouth
a letter said with a thin, light mouth

starter: Say seen, sheen, raa, zay.
Which letters have three dots above?
Show a big round mouth.

teach.heading: Heavy partners
bullets: ص is the heavy partner of س
ض is the heavy partner of د
ط is the heavy partner of ت
ظ is the heavy partner of ذ
teach.note: Introduce 'big mouth' voice. Say seen then Saad; feel the tongue rise and the mouth fill. Do not over-explain; the sound is heard and copied.

teach.heading: Saad and Daad (ص ض)
bullets: ص Saad: round belly, no dot
ض Daad: round belly, one dot above
Fill the mouth when you say them
teach.note: Compare sizes: small seen and big Saad. Daad is a unique Arabic sound; model repeatedly. Accept approximations at this age.

teach.heading: Taa and DHaa (ط ظ)
bullets: ط Taa: loop with a tall stick, no dot
ظ DHaa: loop with a tall stick, one dot
teach.note: Compare with ت (taa) and ذ (dhaal). Ask: which one has a loop? Heavy letters start with the mouth round and tongue raised.

teach.heading: Light or heavy?
bullets: Show a thin mouth for light
Show a round mouth for heavy
teach.note: Say ت then ط, س then ص, ذ then ظ. Children show the mouth shape. Fun, but keep it short.

practice: Is س light or heavy? Is ص light or heavy?
Say ط with a big mouth
independent: Pair cards: light letter with its heavy partner
Trace the four heavy letters
Mouth-shape mirror game
exit: What is the heavy partner of ت?
lessons.homework: Look in a mirror and practise 'big mouth' and 'thin mouth' letters.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use the visual of a balloon (heavy) vs a straw (light). Stretch: write all four heavy letters with their dots.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Arabic letters and their sounds
lessons.title: Letters: 'ayn, ghayn, faa, qaaf, kaaf
objectives: Recognise ع غ ف ق ك
Say the sound of each letter
Find the right dot or dots

keywords.def: a deep throat sound, no English match
a gargling throat sound

starter: Say the heavy letters ص ض ط ظ.
Which light letter pairs with ص?
What is the sound of ج?

teach.heading: 'Ayn and Ghayn (ع غ)
teach.note: 'Ayn is a deep, squeezed sound from the middle of the throat; ghayn is like gargling. Do not force; model and praise effort.

teach.heading: Faa and Qaaf (ف ق)
bullets: ف faa: one dot above, says 'f'
ق qaaf: two dots above, deep 'q'
Qaaf comes from the back of the tongue
teach.note: Faa is the lip-teeth sound, like 'fan'. Qaaf is deeper than 'k'. Make both sounds side by side.

teach.heading: Kaaf (ك)
bullets: Lips relaxed, tongue touches the roof further forward
Different from qaaf: lighter and softer
teach.note: Keep simple. Compare kaaf and qaaf. Ask the class to say kite and Qur'an to hear the difference.

teach.heading: Dot detective
bullets: ف one above, ق two above
teach.note: Display the five letters; ask for dot counts. Many children confuse ف and ق: highlight the dots.

practice: Say the sound of ق and ك
Which letter has one dot and comes from the throat?
independent: Trace ع غ ف ق ك
Sound bingo
Sort letters into throat letters and others
lessons.homework: Say 'Qur'an' slowly and feel where qaaf sounds in the mouth.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: show mouth position diagrams and keep sessions short. Stretch: write two lines of the five letters.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Arabic letters and their sounds
lessons.title: Letters: laam, meem, noon, haa, waaw, yaa, hamza
objectives: Recognise ل م ن ه و ي ء
Say the sounds
Read the whole alphabet in order

keywords.def: a small sound from the throat like a stop
all the letters in order

starter: Say the throat letters ع غ.
Which letter says 'f'?
Which letters are heavy?

teach.heading: Laam, Meem, Noon (ل م ن)
bullets: ن noon: bowl with one dot above
teach.note: Say the letters and compare shapes. Meem closes the lips; laam touches the tongue to the roof; noon touches the tongue near the front teeth.

teach.heading: Haa, Waaw, Yaa (ه و ي)
bullets: ي yaa: two dots below, says 'y'
teach.note: Haa is lighter than ح. Waaw and yaa can also be long vowels later. Keep to the sounds for now.

teach.heading: Hamza (ء)
bullets: ء hamza is a small stop in the throat
teach.note: The English 'uh-oh' sound is a hamza. Children enjoy this. Keep it very simple.

teach.heading: The whole alphabet
bullets: Sing or chant them in order
ا ب ت ث ج ح خ
teach.note: Chant the alphabet in order, pointing. Celebrate. Record on tracker who can say all letters in order; this is the foundation for Year 1.

practice: Say the alphabet from alif to thaa
Which letter has two dots below?
independent: Alphabet puzzle: put the 28 letters in order
Trace ل م ن ه و ي
Read a row of letters with a partner
exit: Which letter has two dots below?
lessons.homework: Chant the alphabet to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use an alphabet strip with pictures. Stretch: say the alphabet backwards from yaa.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Short vowels and first reading
lessons.title: Fathah: the short 'a'
objectives: Know the fathah mark
Say 'a' sounds: ba, ta, tha
Read ب ت ث with fathah

keywords.def: short vowel marks
a small slanted line above a letter, says 'a'

starter: Say the alphabet to the end.
Which letters have dots below?
Say 'baa' with your best lips.

teach.heading: Fathah
bullets: The fathah is a small line above
بَ ba, تَ ta, ثَ tha
teach.note: Draw a hat on the letter. Short means quick: not 'baa', just 'ba'. Clap the quick sound. Many children stretch the sound; model a short, crisp one.

teach.heading: Reading with fathah
teach.note: Say the first letters together, then in mixed order. Point to the letter, then the line above, then say the sound.

teach.heading: Fathah game
bullets: Hold the vowel too long and it changes
teach.note: Stretch deliberately and then say 'no, quick!' to illustrate. Explain that in Qur'an recitation, length is important and will be learned later (madd).

teach.heading: Read the row
teach.note: Children read a row aloud. Stretch: read without the teacher modelling first.

practice: Read: بَ تَ ثَ
What sound does the fathah make?
independent: Read rows of letters with fathah
Trace fathah on ten letters
Fathah flashcards in pairs
exit: What is the mark above called?
lessons.homework: Practise reading 'ba ta tha' to your family.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: tap the rhythm on the table for each short sound. Stretch: read mixed rows quickly.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Short vowels and first reading
lessons.title: Kasrah and Dammah
objectives: Know kasrah (i) and dammah (u)
Read ب ت ث with each mark
Tell the three marks apart

keywords.def: a small slanted line below a letter, says 'i'
a small curl above a letter, says 'u'

starter: Read: بَ تَ ثَ
What is the name of the mark that says 'a'?
Say alif, baa, taa.

teach.heading: Kasrah
bullets: Kasrah is a small line below
بِ bi, تِ ti, ثِ thi
teach.note: Draw a line under the letter. Remind: kasrah sits below, like a sinking letter. 'i' as in 'it'. Keep it short.

teach.heading: Dammah
bullets: Dammah is a small curl above
بُ bu, تُ tu, ثُ thu
teach.note: Dammah looks like a small waaw or a curl above. 'u' as in 'put'. Round the lips slightly. Model.

teach.heading: Three marks together
bullets: بَ ba, بِ bi, بُ bu
Fathah above, kasrah below, dammah curl
teach.note: Chant ba-bi-bu pointing to each. Then other letters. This is the key reading skill for Year 1.

teach.heading: Spot the mark
teach.note: Quick-fire game. Slow down; give thinking time. Record who needs extra practice.

practice: Read: بَ بِ بُ
Which mark goes below the letter?
independent: Read rows with all three marks
Match mark names to sounds
Make a three-mark poster
lessons.homework: Practise 'ba bi bu' with a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour-code the marks. Stretch: write a letter with each of the three marks.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Short vowels and first reading
lessons.title: Reading together and An-Nas (ayah 1)
objectives: Blend letters and marks into syllables
Listen to An-Nas ayah 1
Echo ayah 1 with the teacher

keywords.def: join sounds together to read
the 114th and last surah of the Qur'an

starter: Read: بَ بِ بُ
Name the three marks.
What is the last surah of the Qur'an?

teach.heading: Blending
bullets: Read syllable by syllable, then together
teach.note: Choose easy blends like ba-ta, ka-ta, la-ma. Point to each syllable. Lift your voice slightly on the last syllable to show the end of the word.

teach.heading: An-Nas: the last surah
bullets: Our final surah to listen to
teach.note: Say that An-Nas and Al-Falaq are surahs we seek protection with. Do not go into detail beyond meaning. Link to Allah protecting us.

teach.heading: Ayah 1
bullets: Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind
teach.note: Chunk: Qul / a'udhu / bi-Rabbin-naas. Explain a'udhu = I seek protection with. Ask: who protects us? Allah.

teach.heading: End-of-term review
teach.note: Informal check: each child reads three syllables aloud and recites Al-Fatihah in chunks. Record tracker scores (1-3) and who needs extra support.

practice: Read: مَ لَ
Echo 'Qul a'udhu bi Rabbin-naas'
independent: Read syllables in pairs, then to the teacher
Colour the letters of 'An-Nas'
Chant ayah 1 to a rhythm
lessons.homework: Tell your family the name of the last surah and say its first ayah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: build words with letter tiles. Stretch: read a new three-syllable string.
